identification: NtHook kernel bootkit carrying a recovery driver and Gh0st-derived safemon.dll
method: Independent static review with cleave facts, atomscan, Rizin disassembly, and PE/real-mode decoding with pefile and Capstone. No sample or derivative was executed. Scanner scores and earlier review notes were not used to establish behavior.
evidence: Driver entry 0x000a803e reaches 0x0001586c and initialization 0x00015262. Initialization writes the embedded recovery image, the main driver and safemon.dll, initializes syscall interception, obtains the disk device and calls the boot installation routine.

Driver 0x00012f00 reads sector zero, stages code and PE images in additional disk sectors, and writes a replacement boot-code prefix back to disk offset zero at 0x0001332f. Wrapper 0x00012dd2 constructs IRPs with IoBuildAsynchronousFsdRequest and dispatches them through IofCallDriver; major function 3 reads and 4 writes. Device acquisition 0x00012cf6 resolves the Windows disk driver object.

Embedded 16-bit code at driver VA 0x000187d0 lowers the BIOS conventional-memory size, relocates itself and replaces INT 13h's IVT entry. The handler chains the original disk-read service, scans its returned buffer for boot-code instruction patterns, and patches it with a relocated CALL FAR or indirect-call transfer before restoring the interrupt vector. These are boot interception and payload execution, not merely MBR vocabulary.

Syscall dispatcher 0x00013d7e routes selected native functions to replacement handlers. Directory-query handler 0x0001334a calls the original, compares returned names with the private list and removes matches by relinking or copying subsequent entries over them. Initialization adds NtHook.sys, safemon.dll and its INI names to that list through 0x000122ba.

The embedded 5632-byte recovery driver starts at outer offset 0x7788. Its entry reaches 0x0001127e, reads sector zero and hidden-sector payload data, checks the recovered image for MZ, writes NtHook.sys, configures its kernel service and invokes ZwLoadDriver. This provides a concrete recovery path for disk-staged payloads.

The 256512-byte DLL at outer offset 0x8d88 exports hook2. Its 0x10005eb0 path enables debug privilege, searches for explorer.exe, allocates target-process memory, writes a DLL pathname and reaches remote-thread setup. Its keyboard manager starts routine 0x1000e290, which polls key states, interprets modifiers and editing keys, and forwards text to 0x1000e050. Foreground-window context is collected by 0x1000e180.

DLL 0x1000e050 constructs a log filename from stack byte stores and XORs captured text with 0x62 into a new buffer; 0x1000e14f hands that output buffer to the indirect write routine. DLL 0x10010a30 resolves GetClipboardData(CF_TEXT), locks its returned handle and copies the text after a record tag. The manager RTTI corroborates Gh0st lineage; it is not the sole basis for conviction.

IsDebuggerPresent is called in DLL routines 0x1001ae97 and 0x1001b6b4 alongside exception codes 0xc0000417 and 0xc0000409, exception-filter handling and process termination. These are CRT invalid-parameter/security-failure paths; the import does not establish deliberate analysis evasion.

Facts include wide strings and Base64-decoded candidates. The latter are short noisy decodings of byte runs; the traced concealment relevant here is the XOR log transform, runtime API resolution, boot redirection and selective directory-result suppression. The embedded executable images can be recovered directly without unpacking.

The unsigned driver claims Microsoft Windows Player identity, which does not explain boot-code installation, self-concealment and the bundled recorder. The original package, installer authorization, operator and host execution history are unavailable. The combined implemented behavior supports malicious treatment even without inventing that deployment context.
changes: Relocated the unsigned/debugger/allocation/remote-write combination from the hostile injection objective to a notable memory-write API profile. Preserved its matching scope and exclusions; removed unsupported anti-debugging and injection technique claims.

Added notable imported IRP-builder/dispatcher and disk-driver pathname facts plus a neutral raw-disk I/O profile. The profile explicitly does not claim a linked write or boot overwrite. Added native NtWriteFile/ZwWriteFile import coverage.

Moved ZwCreateKey from hive to key access and native registry value writers to write. Kept these operations notable even when version resources claim Microsoft. Removed the unreferenced registry-persistence-primitives composite because three generic APIs provide no reactivation trigger; its atomic observations remain available.

Audited the full access/write leaf populations at their existing budgets. Moved two Python key-creation rules from write to access, and StubPath/ServiceDLL value-name observations from access to value-name. Matchers and effective scopes are preserved. Updated every exact YAML consumer. Both access and write finish at 100 rules, without a new split or budget override.

Ancestor-selector audit: the registry ancestor still selects the relocated registry facts; the PowerShell-only injection selector cannot consume the moved PE-only API profile. Native value writes are appropriate new members of write-directory consumers. Pure Python key creation no longer satisfies the ComputerDefaults consumer's value-write requirement; a focused negative case checks this correction. Value names no longer serve as registry-access evidence solely by access-directory membership.

verification.controls: Renamed original, real recorder, import-only DLL with no hostile or suspicious findings, missing debugger/remote-write imports, independently missing disk/profile legs, missing native writer, Python key creation versus read, value-name near miss, and key-creation-only UAC near miss.
